fact_text: When you leave Ireland and may become non-resident for Irish tax, Revenue recommends updating your contact details in myAccount/ROS to a non-Republic-of-Ireland address; if you leave your job before leaving, it is your employer's responsibility to cease your employment with Revenue, and if they fail to do so you can cease it yourself in myAccount.
evidence_quote: If you are leaving your job before leaving Ireland, it is the responsibility of your employer to cease your employment with Revenue.

fact_text: In the year you leave Ireland you can claim 'split-year treatment' on employment income if you are resident in your year of departure and not resident the following year: income up to your departure date is taxed normally and employment income earned abroad after departure is ignored for Irish tax. You apply in writing via MyEnquiries in myAccount or to your Revenue office.
evidence_quote: You can claim ‘split-year treatment’ on your employment income for the year you depart Ireland if you are: resident in your year of departure and not resident in Ireland the following year.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Split-year treatment covers employment income only and requires non-residence the following year; it is claimed in writing, not automatic.

fact_text: You are Irish tax-resident for a year if you spend 183 days or more in Ireland that year, or 280 days or more across two consecutive tax years (with a minimum of 31 days in each year). Even after leaving you remain 'ordinarily resident' until you have been non-resident for 3 continuous tax years.
evidence_quote: You are resident for tax purposes for a year if you spend 183 days or more in Ireland in that year.Alternatively, if you spend 280 days or more in Ireland over a period of 2 consecutive tax years, you will be regarded as resident for the second tax year.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Ordinary residence lingers for 3 years after departure, so Irish tax exposure on certain income can continue even once the mover is back in Spain.

fact_text: A PPS number is not reissued: if you already have one (e.g. from having worked in Ireland) you do not need to apply for a new one, so a mover leaving Ireland keeps their existing PPSN for any future Irish social welfare or Revenue dealings.
evidence_quote: If you already have a PPS number, you do not need to apply for a new one.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The PPSN persists after emigration; there is no baja/surrender step for it, unlike the Irish immigration permission.

fact_text: On returning to Spain, anyone living in Spain is obliged to register (empadronarse) in the padrón of the municipality where they habitually reside; if they live in more than one municipality they register where they spend most of the year. In Madrid this is done online with electronic ID or in person by appointment at a Citizen Attention Office.
evidence_quote: Toda persona que viva en España está obligada a inscribirse en el Padrón del municipio donde reside habitualmente. Quien viva en más de un municipio se inscribirá en el que resida durante más tiempo al año.

fact_text: A returning third-country national (non-EU) empadronamiento in Madrid requires original, in-force identity documents: a residence permit, or the passport if no residence permit is held. The town hall may require an official sworn translation of documents issued by foreign authorities.
evidence_quote: De otras nacionalidades: permiso de residencia (si no se dispone de él, se aportará el pasaporte).

fact_text: To be registered (alta) in the Spanish Social Security system for the first time when starting work, you need a Social Security Number (NUSS, also called NAF); it is also used by your region's health system to set up your health card. Any citizen without an assigned number can request it at any time.
evidence_quote: Necesitarás el NUSS para darte de alta por primera vez en la Seguridad Social cuando inicies tu actividad laboral y para acceder a pensiones, subsidios y prestaciones.

fact_text: On re-establishing life in Spain you become a Spanish tax resident under domestic law if you spend more than 183 days of the calendar year in Spain, or your main base of economic activities/interests is in Spain; the change of residence does not interrupt the tax period, so you are resident or non-resident for the whole calendar year.
evidence_quote: Que permanezca en España más de 183 días durante el año natural. Para determinar este período de permanencia se computan sus ausencias esporádicas, salvo que acredite su residencia fiscal en otro país.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Because both Spain and Ireland can each claim residence in the return year, a treaty tie-breaker (permanent home, centre of vital interests) determines the outcome.

fact_text: If returning to (or remaining a national abroad from) Venezuela, inscription in the Consular Registry constitutes a census of Venezuelans abroad and is a duty for those residing in the consulate's jurisdiction; being registered in the Consular Registry is required in order to carry out any procedure before the Venezuelan consulate.
evidence_quote: El registro consular constituye un censo de venezolanos y venezolanas en el exterior y es un deber para todos los que residentes en Cataluña, Aragón, Islas Baleares y Comunidad Valenciana. Para la realización de cualquier trámite ante este Consulado General es necesario estar inscrito en el Registro Consular.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The quoted jurisdiction (Cataluña/Aragón/Baleares/Valencia) is the Barcelona consulate's; a Madrid-based mover would register at the competent Venezuelan consulate for Madrid, but the census/duty rule and the 'required for any procedure' rule are the same official framework. Fee stated as gratuito.
